items.title: build_kv_chunk_table assumes every layer holds a KV slab, so no hybrid-attention model can be PCC-checked through the runner
items.body:
Found during Kimi-K3 runner bring-up (#53508). Index: #54814.

## What

Publishing the KV chunk table asserts that the cache's batch dimension equals `num_users * num_my_layers`:

```
AssertionError: cache batch dim 6 != num_users(1) * num_my_layers(24)
```

Kimi-K3 is hybrid: only 24 of its 93 layers are full-attention (MLA); the other 69 are KDA and write no KV slab at all. A 24-layer slice therefore holds **6** MLA layers and allocates 6 cache entries, not 24. The assertion rejects the model outright.

`KimiK3Adapter.allocate_kv_cache` already sizes the cache by `schedule.num_mla_layers` rather than `params.num_layers` — correctly. The table builder is the piece that still assumes one slab per layer.

## Why it matters

This is the only path to scoring PCC on what the runner actually produces. `prefill_producer` locates each cache through the published table (`_read_kv_chunk_table` -> `_verify_resident_slots` -> `_read_slot_kv_and_check_pcc_mla`) and reads it back over UMD. No table, no read-back, no PCC.

Combined with `PREFILL_MOCK_MIGRATION` refusing `num_ranks>1` (each rank would publish a table covering only its own slice), **there is currently no configuration in which a hybrid model can be accuracy-checked end to end through the runner** — multi-rank is refused by design, and single-rank fails this assertion.

Consequences for Kimi-K3 today:

- correctness had to be established **in-process** instead (two transformers on one mesh, output piped directly), which verifies the model but not the socket path
- the `PREFILL_USE_TRACE=1` replay cannot be PCC-checked at all, so tracing has no verified-correct measurement despite capturing and replaying cleanly

## Repro

Any hybrid-attention model, single rank:

```
PREFILL_MOCK_MIGRATION=1 ./models/demos/common/prefill/runners/run_pipeline_prefill.sh \
  <a kimi_k3 rank binding> <host>:1 <iface>
```

Fails during table publish, before serving.

## Suggested fix

Size the table from the same source the cache was allocated from — the model's layer schedule (`num_mla_layers` / the per-layer KV-slot map) rather than the rank's layer count. The adapter already exposes it; the assertion just needs to ask for it instead of assuming a dense stack.

items.title: AttnRes weight loading ignores first_layer_idx: a pipeline rank silently loads another rank's queries
items.body:
Found during Kimi-K3 2-rank bring-up (#53508). Index: #54814. Fixed on `feature/kimi-k3-prefill`.

## What

`load_attn_res_weights` took the rank-LOCAL layer count and no offset, while the tensorbin cache and the checkpoint are both keyed by GLOBAL layer index. A rank holding layers 36..71 asked for `layers.0..35`.

Every name it asked for exists — the cache holds all 93 layers — so `check_cache_complete` returned True and the rank came up **scoring every AttnRes read with another rank's query**. No error, no warning, a plausible model.

## Why it survived

Nothing catches it:

- the cache is complete for the names requested, so the completeness check passes
- the shapes are identical (one folded query per layer), so nothing downstream objects
- single-rank runs have `first_layer_idx = 0`, where local and global indices coincide — so the entire existing suite is blind to it by construction

## Fix

Thread `first_layer_idx` through the naming and the checkpoint fold:

- [`_cache_artifact_names`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/752fce2c47b63470a83724c689011d17af5b86ee/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tt/attn_res/weights.py#L35) — `layers.{first_layer_idx + idx}`
- [`check_cache_complete`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/752fce2c47b63470a83724c689011d17af5b86ee/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tt/attn_res/weights.py#L100) — same window, or it verifies someone else's files are present
- [`load_attn_res_weights`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/752fce2c47b63470a83724c689011d17af5b86ee/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tt/attn_res/weights.py#L174) — offset in `place(...)`
- `fold_queries` / `query_weight_names` / `validate_query_weights` in `reference/kimi_k3/attn_res/weights.py` — same, for the state-dict path

Pinned by hardware-free tests in `tests/attn_res/model/test_attn_res_pipeline_split.py`, including that two ranks request **disjoint** windows (sharing only the model-level `output` query).

## Related

Same local-vs-global confusion as #54843. A third instance: `schedule.mla_layer_ids` is the whole MODEL's list, so the common `mla_layer_ids[:num_mla_layers]` idiom yields 3/7/11 for every rank and is correct only at `first_layer_idx = 0` — it scored a rank-1 layer-15 KV slab against layer 3's golden and reported PCC 0.006. Worth auditing every `first_layer_idx`-adjacent accessor for the same shape of bug.

items.title: prefill_producer: reported throughput measures push rate, not model throughput, and overstates it ~3x
items.body:
Found during Kimi-K3 runner bring-up (#53508). Index: #54814.

## What

The headline line every bring-up quotes is [`throughput={total_tokens / stats.wall_s}`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_producer.py#L1471). `wall_s` is set in `run_schedule` as [`wall_s=now_fn() - start`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_producer.py#L704) — it covers **only the push loop**.

The ack drain that establishes the device actually finished runs afterwards, at [prefill_producer.py#L1479](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_producer.py#L1479), outside the timer. And the ack channel is only opened when `cfg.verify` is set: [`ack_channel = _connect_layer_ack_channel(timeout_s) if cfg.verify else None`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_producer.py#L1434).

So with the common `PREFILL_PRODUCER_CHECK_PCC=0` the producer is a pure token feeder (its own log says so), nothing waits for completion, and `throughput` is the rate at which the H2D queue **absorbed** chunks. Deep enough queue, and it measures the queue.

## Observed

Kimi-K3, 72 layers, 2 ranks, 11 chunks of 5120 (55k tokens), untraced. Same run, three clocks:

| measurement | result | what it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| producer, cold | 2576 tok/s | push loop, including first-chunk compile |
| producer, warm | 11737 tok/s | push loop only — **3.0x** the real figure |
| device signposts | **3937 tok/s** | first to last signpost, 14.3 s, 1301 ms/chunk |

The device number is corroborated: exactly 18 `MLA_START` and 70 `MoE_START` per chunk across all 11 chunks, so the window contains all the work and nothing else.

The warm figure is the dangerous one — it is stable, reproducible across runs (11669 / 11749 / 11737), and implies a 72-layer model outrunning a measured 24-layer configuration. It looks like a good result rather than a broken metric.

## Suggested fix

Either stop the clock after the acks are drained, or rename the field to something that cannot be mistaken for model throughput (`push_rate`). Reporting a tok/s number that excludes the model is worse than reporting none, because it silently becomes the number people quote.

items.title: prefill runner: LayerAck FIFO default (341 records) is smaller than one run's ack count, so the drain can never complete
items.body:
Found during Kimi-K3 runner bring-up (#53508). Index: #54814.

## What

[`LAYER_ACK_FIFO_SIZE_BYTES`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_runner.py#L95) defaults to 4 KB, and records are [`METADATA_SIZE_BYTES = 12`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_runner.py#L91) bytes — **341 slots**.

The producer waits for `NUM_LAYERS * pushes` acks: [`_drain_layer_acks(ack_channel, NUM_LAYERS * stats.total_pushes)`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_producer.py#L1479). A 72-layer, 11-chunk run expects **792**, which exceeds the ring by 2.3x.

Crucially the drain is called **after** the push loop finishes, not concurrently with it, so by the time anything is consumed the runner has long since emitted more than 341 records and the oldest are gone. The expected count is then unreachable and the drain always burns its full timeout.

## Observed

72 layers, 11 chunks of 5120 (55k tokens), 2 ranks:

```
[producer] drained 207/792 layer acks in 600.01s
```

The work itself completed — device signposts show exactly 18 `MLA_START` and 70 `MoE_START` per chunk over all 11 chunks. Only the acks were lost, so this reads as a hang or a stalled device when it is neither.

## Repro

Any run where `NUM_LAYERS * chunks > 341`, with `PREFILL_PRODUCER_CHECK_PCC=1` (which is what opens the channel at [prefill_producer.py#L1434](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_producer.py#L1434)).

## Workaround

`PREFILL_LAYER_ACK_FIFO_BYTES=65536` (5461 records). The env override already exists; only the default is wrong.

## Suggested fix

The comment at [prefill_runner.py#L93-L94](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/b069c3c794abeebe413fd8b1c2eab4bc193cf176/models/demos/common/prefill/runners/prefill_runner.py#L93-L94) calls 4 KB "generous headroom for in-flight records", which holds only if the consumer keeps up. Either size the default from `NUM_LAYERS` and the expected in-flight chunk count, drain concurrently with the push loop, or make overflow loud — a dropped-record counter would turn a 600 s silent timeout into an immediate diagnosis.

items.title: ttnn.digamma FLOAT32 is ~4,500 ULP off for x > 102
items.body:
`ttnn.digamma` supports positive `BFLOAT16` and `FLOAT32` inputs. The
FLOAT32 path is thousands of ULP off for inputs above 102.

## Results

ttsim Blackhole, 4,094 geometrically spaced FLOAT32 inputs in `[102, 3.0e38]`,
`dest_acc=Yes`. Reference: the LLK harness golden, which is `torch.digamma`
evaluated in FLOAT32. I injected `-DINP_FLOAT32`, which TTNN sets for FLOAT32
inputs but the LLK test harness does not.

Since that golden is itself FLOAT32, I checked it against an independent 60-digit
computation: on the points cited below it is bit-exact. This measures the kernel,
not the reference. As a control that the define is in effect, the FLOAT32 branch
measures 1 median ULP on `[0.01, 102]`, where the BFLOAT16 branch measures 48.

| | Current kernel | With fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median ULP | 4,543 | 0 |
| p99 ULP | 8,403 | 1 |
| Max ULP | 9,080 | 1 |
| Max relative error | 6.86e-04 | 1.19e-07 |
| Bit-exact results | 1 / 4,094 | 3,930 / 4,094 |

Example:

```
x = 1820.104
reference = 7.50637436
current   = 7.50204468  (9,080 ULP)
fixed     = 7.50637436  (bit-exact)
```

The error is not limited to the largest inputs. Median error is 3,864 ULP on
`[102, 200)`, 5,019 ULP on `[200, 1e3)`, and 4,386 ULP above `1e12`.

## Cause

For `x > 102`, `ckernel_sfpu_digamma.h` uses the Bernoulli asymptotic and calls
`_calculate_log_body_no_init_`. That log body uses:

```
sfpi::vFloat vConstLn2 = 0.692871f;
```

The constant has a `-3.98e-04` relative error. The same body also uses a
third-order mantissa polynomial. At the worst point, the constant accounts for
64% of the error and the polynomial for 36%. Replacing only the constant still
leaves about 176 median ULP in the host model.

The kernel comment says the accurate log body cannot be used because its program
constants conflict with the reciprocal. Calling that body does conflict. The
algorithm itself does not: the same range reduction and FLOAT32 coefficients can
use immediate constants and no program constant registers.

The same branch also returns `89.09284` for `digamma(NaN)`. Its guard handles
infinity but excludes NaN.

## Proposed fix

I have a patch for Blackhole and Wormhole that:

1. uses an immediate-only accurate log body for `INP_FLOAT32`;
2. passes NaN and infinity through;
3. adds TTNN tests for large FLOAT32 inputs, NaN, and infinity.

The `[0.01, 102]` range is bit-identical before and after on both dtypes. The
BFLOAT16 large-x path is unchanged. Static instruction counts for the FLOAT32
path increase by 5.7% on Blackhole and 4.3% on Wormhole. The BFLOAT16 paths
become shorter.

I tested the kernel with ttsim for Blackhole and Wormhole. I do not have
Tenstorrent hardware, so the TTNN device test has not been run.

## Prior work

#51129 changes the same files for the `x < 0.01` recurrence. It does not change
the `x > 102` branch. I rechecked current `main` at `b069c3c794ab`; the two
digamma kernel files are unchanged from my patch base.

Could you please assign this to me?

items.title: Environment and data traps: mesh poisoning after kill -9, transposed golden KDA state, mesh-axis dim order

labels.name: shield_prefill
labels.description: Prefill tasks worked on by Shield team

items.body:
Sub-issue of #54814. Hit during Kimi-K3 bring-up (#53508).

Four unrelated traps that each cost real debugging time and are invisible from the code.

**1. `kill -9` on a process holding the 32-chip mesh poisons the next process.** The command queues and fabric are left in a state the next process inherits, and the symptom is indistinguishable from a model hang — sixteen minutes blocked inside a plain `ttnn.from_torch → enqueue_write_shards → wait_for_outstanding_reads`, with no AttnRes code involved at all. `tt-smi -glx_reset` (~90 s) clears it. SIGTERM during mesh *open* also strands ethernet cores ("Timed out while waiting for active ethernet core 22-25"). Rule adopted: stop device runs with SIGTERM or let the pytest timeout fire, and confirm any suspected hang on a freshly reset device before recording it as a finding.

**2. The golden trace stores the KDA recurrent state transposed relative to the reference.** Golden is `[heads, v_dim, k_dim]`, the reference `[heads, k_dim, v_dim]`. Both are `[96, 128, 128]`, so omitting the transpose reports PCC 0.012 — indistinguishable from a broken recurrence rather than from a layout mistake.

**3. `ConcatMesh2dToTensor` / `ShardTensor2dMesh` take dims in mesh-axis order.** Passing them swapped composes a tensor of the correct shape out of the wrong pieces and reads as PCC 0.03. Not an error, and nothing in the result points at the composer.

**4. Pre-existing on the bring-up box:** 2–3 `sigmoid_gated_rms_norm` production-perf tests fail with the **stock** kernel, unmodified. Unrelated to Kimi-K3, but they will be misattributed by anyone bisecting a K3 change.

items.title: Five coverage blind spots let the KDA t_inv defect (#54813) pass every existing test

labels.name: shield_prefill
labels.description: Prefill tasks worked on by Shield team

items.body:
Sub-issue of #54814. Hit during Kimi-K3 bring-up (#53508).

#54813 was a total failure — the KDA layer uncorrelated with its own reference on 68 of Kimi-K3's 69 KDA layers — and every existing test passed. Five independent blind spots, each worth fixing on its own terms because the same shapes will hide the next defect.

**1. `t_inv` is scored by whole-tensor PCC.** It is `I + strictly-lower`, so PCC is dominated by the identity diagonal. The broken output scored **0.99508**, above the suite's own 0.999 bar, while its strictly-lower part — the entire content of the UT transform — scored **0.935**. Any threshold on this output belongs on the strictly-lower part, not the whole tile.

**2. `_host_inputs` pins the gate to `[-0.051, -0.001]`.** Kimi-K3's gate is `KDA_GATE_LOWER_BOUND * sigmoid(...)` with a lower bound of -5.0, spanning `(-5, 0)` — two orders of magnitude outside coverage, and exactly the regime the defect lives in.

**3. `host_protocol` pins every other magnitude too:** `final_decay` to [0.86, 0.94], the strict-lower block feeding `t_inv` to 0.015, `kd`/`k_dec_t` to 0.025. Every scan case draws from one point in a seven-dimensional magnitude space.

**4. `make_kimi_k3_test_case` pairs real weights with `torch.randn` activations.** `test_kimi_k3_layer_1_real_weights_pcc` exercises the exact layer the defect breaks and passes at 0.9995. **Nothing tested real weights against real activations** — the only combination where blind spots 2/3 and the real data meet.

**5. The `invert_doubling` comment stated its own stability claim "must be validated empirically."** It never was, so the defect sat documented-as-unverified in-tree for the life of the op.

Two op-level suites were added during the bring-up covering the magnitudes (1)-(3) never generate.

items.title: attn_res_gather_softmax deadlocks under Topology::Ring, so AttnRes cannot run on FABRIC_2D_TORUS_XY

labels.name: shield_prefill
labels.description: Prefill tasks worked on by Shield team

items.body:
Sub-issue of #54814. Hit during Kimi-K3 bring-up (#53508).

AttnRes hangs on `FABRIC_2D_TORUS_XY`, the production fabric for a Blackhole Galaxy. Isolated across four runs on a freshly reset device:

| fabric | payload | result |
|---|---|---|
| `FABRIC_2D` | 4352 B | passes, worst PCC 0.9999948, 91 s |
| `FABRIC_2D_TORUS_XY` | 14336 B (max) | hangs |
| `FABRIC_2D_TORUS_XY` | 7168 B (K3's own) | hangs |
| `FABRIC_2D_TORUS_XY`, `Topology::Linear` forced | 7168 B | hangs |

So it is not the mesh width (Fabric2D at 8x4 passes with an 8-wide sequence axis), not the payload, and not the `topology` argument. `FABRIC_2D_TORUS_Y` — which would give `(Ring, Linear)` and keep AttnRes's exchange off the wrapped axis — is rejected at 8x4 as an unfeasible fabric/mesh combination, so there is no middle ground.

**Stack when hung:** main thread in `ttnn::cpu → enqueue_read_tensor → wait_for_outstanding_reads`, completion-queue reader spinning in `completion_queue_wait_front`. The op was enqueued and never completed.

**Mechanism, from the program factory:** under `Ring`, `attn_res_gather_softmax_program_factory.cpp:112-119` gives rank 0 a backward neighbour and rank N-1 a forward one, closing the connection graph into a cycle that every rank then sends across to all `ring_size - 1` peers. Under `Linear` that graph is acyclic and cannot deadlock this way.

**Workaround:** run Kimi-K3 entirely on `FABRIC_2D`. The rest of the model is certified on TorusXY, so this is AttnRes's constraint alone.

CI could not have caught it: every AttnRes arm, suite and op-level, was 2x4 Fabric2D.

items.title: SDPA reads zero-padded mask columns when Sk % 32 != 0
items.body:
## Summary

On Wormhole with tt-metal `66a55a6fbee`,
`ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention` returned incorrect BF16 output
under these conditions:

- we supplied an explicit BF16 `attn_mask`;
- we created the mask with `ttnn.from_torch`, which pads TILE tensors with zero
  by default; and
- the key sequence length was not a multiple of the 32-element tile width. We
  tested S=16 and S=40.

Changing only the mask's physical padding to negative infinity fixed the
result:

```python
pad_value=float("-inf")
```

At S=16 and S=40, the fixed output was bit-for-bit identical to the accurate
`is_causal=True` device control. At the tile-aligned length S=32, both padding
values produced the correct output. At S=16, repeated calls confirmed that
both the failure and the fix were deterministic.

The results also separate physical padding from the mask's logical values. At
S=16, S=32, and S=40, logical upper-triangle values of `-1e9` and `-inf`
produced bit-for-bit identical output. Both values failed when the physical
padding remained zero. This shows that SDPA reads the zero-valued columns in
the final partial mask tile.

## Why this matters

PR #36170 documents support for provided masks at arbitrary non-chunk-aligned
Q/K lengths. A caller following that contract can receive a well-formed tensor
with severely incorrect values when `ttnn.from_torch` uses its default tile
padding. Applications need explicit masks for behavior that
`is_causal=True` cannot express, including additive bias, padding, and token
selection. We found this bug while implementing sparse-selection attention.

## Environment

- tt-metal / TTNN: `66a55a6fbee8bccba60a8225bd10aece6f62e556`
  (`v0.76.0-dev20260728-18-g66a55a6fbee`)
- Firmware bundle: `19.13.1`
- Kernel driver: `2.10.0`
- Hardware: Wormhole Galaxy, one host-facing ASIC at `0000:c6:00.0`, PCIe
  Gen4 x8
- Isolation: exclusive lease, `TT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=29`, process-local device 0
- Python: CPython `3.10.19`
- Q/K/V and mask: BF16 TILE layout
- Shape: Q `[1,24,S,256]`; K/V `[1,2,S,256]`; mask `[1,1,S,S]`
- Scale: `1/sqrt(256) = 0.0625`
- Seed: `20260829`
- Reference: PyTorch MATH SDPA with BF16-rounded Q/K/V and BF16-rounded output

Before running the matrix, we reset only `0000:c6:00.0` with
`tt-smi -r`. The reset completed with exit code 0. We then ran an isolated BF16
matmul control, which passed at PCC `0.999988995`.

The SDPA test opened and closed the device cleanly. Its log contained no
unexpected-mailbox, failed-early-exit, stale-dispatch, or
failed-firmware-initialization markers. Before and after the test, `c6`
reported healthy DRAM, live Ethernet, faults `0x0`, throttler `0x0`, and a
temperature range of 26.4–28.0 C.

## Clean test results

The table reports the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), root mean square
error (RMSE), and maximum absolute error against the PyTorch reference.

| S | Case | PCC vs PyTorch | RMSE | max abs | Output comparison |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 16 | no mask | 0.999777249 | 0.0088650 | 0.06640625 | full-attention control |
| 16 | `is_causal=True` | 0.999836732 | 0.0130208 | 0.109375 | causal device control |
| 16 | provided mask, default zero padding | **0.846577666** | **0.3857387** | **3.298828125** | corrupted |
| 16 | provided mask, `pad_value=-inf` | 0.999836732 | 0.0130208 | 0.109375 | **bit-for-bit equal to causal control** |
| 16 | pad Q/K/V/mask to S=32 | 0.999836732 | 0.0130208 | 0.109375 | **bit-for-bit equal for retained rows** |
| 32 | `is_causal=True` | 0.999821368 | 0.0105774 | 0.125 | causal device control |
| 32 | provided mask, default zero padding | 0.999821368 | 0.0105774 | 0.125 | **bit-for-bit equal to causal control** |
| 32 | provided mask, `pad_value=-inf` | 0.999821368 | 0.0105774 | 0.125 | **bit-for-bit equal to causal control** |
| 40 | no mask | 0.999707378 | 0.0068025 | 0.0703125 | full-attention control |
| 40 | `is_causal=True` | 0.999816218 | 0.0104603 | 0.125 | causal device control |
| 40 | provided mask, default zero padding | **0.831548585** | **0.2966589** | **3.808837891** | corrupted |
| 40 | provided mask, `pad_value=-inf` | 0.999816218 | 0.0104603 | 0.125 | **bit-for-bit equal to causal control** |

We compared the complete output hashes to verify every bit-for-bit equality in
the table.

Earlier diagnostic runs showed the same alignment pattern at S=48 (failed) and
S=64 (passed). The clean matrix above is the evidence used for this report. It
covers one seed, one chip, BF16, square self-attention, native grouped-query
attention, and S=16/32/40. We have not tested every non-tile-aligned shape or
every supported mask dtype.

## Minimal reproduction

Isolate the target physical device before importing TTNN. Our physical UMD ID
was 29; use the appropriate ID on another system. Inside the process, the
isolated device is device 0.

```bash
TT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=29 \
TT_METAL_CACHE=/tmp/tt-rt-004-cache \
python repro.py
```

```python
import math
import torch
from torch.nn.attention import SDPBackend, sdpa_kernel
import ttnn

NQH, NKV, DH, S = 24, 2, 256, 16


def pcc(a, b):
    a = a.flatten().double()
    b = b.flatten().double()
    a -= a.mean()
    b -= b.mean()
    return float((a * b).sum() / (a.norm() * b.norm()).clamp_min(1e-12))


def upload(t, device, pad_value=None):
    kwargs = dict(dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, device=device)
    if pad_value is not None:
        kwargs["pad_value"] = pad_value
    return ttnn.from_torch(t, **kwargs)


torch.manual_seed(20260829)
q = torch.randn(1, NQH, S, DH).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
k = torch.randn(1, NKV, S, DH).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
v = torch.randn(1, NKV, S, DH).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
mask = torch.zeros(S, S)
mask.masked_fill_(torch.ones(S, S, dtype=torch.bool).triu(1), -1e9)
mask = mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(DH)

with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH):
    reference = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(
        q,
        k.repeat_interleave(NQH // NKV, dim=1),
        v.repeat_interleave(NQH // NKV, dim=1),
        is_causal=True,
        scale=scale,
    ).to(torch.bfloat16).float()

device = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)
try:
    qt, kt, vt = upload(q, device), upload(k, device), upload(v, device)

    def run(mask_tt=None, is_causal=False):
        out = ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            qt, kt, vt, attn_mask=mask_tt, is_causal=is_causal, scale=scale
        )
        return ttnn.to_torch(out).float()

    causal = run(is_causal=True)
    broken = run(upload(mask, device))
    repaired = run(upload(mask, device, pad_value=float("-inf")))

    print("causal PCC:", pcc(causal, reference))
    print("default-padding PCC:", pcc(broken, reference))
    print("-inf-padding PCC:", pcc(repaired, reference))
    print("repaired equals causal:", torch.equal(repaired, causal))
finally:
    ttnn.close_device(device)
```

Expected output on the affected build is approximately:

```text
causal PCC: 0.99984
default-padding PCC: 0.85
-inf-padding PCC: 0.99984
repaired equals causal: True
```

## Relevant source and upstream changes

This appears to be a missing partial-tile case in the arbitrary-length
provided-mask support requested in
[issue #36097](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/36097) and added
by [PR #36170](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/36170). PR #36170
says that the reader fills padded Q and K mask positions with negative
infinity. Its S=160 test is not chunk-aligned in that test configuration, but
160 is still a multiple of the 32-element tile width. The test therefore does
not cover a partially filled final tile.

[PR #46600](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/46600) later moved
provided dense masks to streaming SDPA. Its reported K-padding tests ran on
Blackhole and do not state whether they covered a partial final tile on
Wormhole.

At the commit we tested, the code handles the mask as follows:

- [`py_to_tt_tensor.cpp`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/66a55a6fbee8bccba60a8225bd10aece6f62e556/ttnn/core/tensor/py_to_tt_tensor.cpp#L442-L454)
  uses `pad_value.value_or(0.0f)`, so a tiled mask has zero-valued physical
  padding unless the caller overrides it.
- [`reader_interleaved.cpp`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/66a55a6fbee8bccba60a8225bd10aece6f62e556/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/transformer/sdpa/device/kernels/dataflow/reader_interleaved.cpp#L521-L556)
  tests `global_k_tile < valid_Skt`. The final partial K tile is therefore
  considered valid and copied in full. Only wholly out-of-range tiles are
  replaced by `fill_neginf_tile`.
- [`sdpa_program_factory.cpp`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/66a55a6fbee8bccba60a8225bd10aece6f62e556/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/transformer/sdpa/device/sdpa_program_factory.cpp#L419-L428)
  enables its partial-column mask only for
  `generated_padding_mask && !use_provided_mask`. The adjacent comment says the
  reader fills padded positions for a dense provided mask, but the reader's
  decision is at whole-tile granularity.

This is not the mask-scaling bug fixed by
[PR #42891](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/42891): that change is
an ancestor of the tested build, aligned S works at the same scale, and the
failure is repaired solely by changing physical padding. It is also not one of
the five SDPA defects grouped in
[issue #51223](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/51223).

## Expected behavior

Values outside a mask's logical S×S shape should not change the SDPA output. If
provided masks with `Sk % 32 != 0` are unsupported, SDPA should reject them
instead of returning a well-formed tensor with incorrect values.

## Verified workarounds

The simplest workaround on the affected build is to initialize the mask's
physical padding to negative infinity:

```python
mask_tt = ttnn.from_torch(
    mask,
    dtype=ttnn.bfloat16,
    layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT,
    device=device,
    pad_value=float("-inf"),
)
```

Padding Q/K/V and the mask to the next multiple of 32 also works, but it
changes the tensor shapes and performs unnecessary work. A causal-only path can
avoid a provided mask and use `is_causal=True`.

items.title: ttnn.softplus_bw forms redundant intermediates around the exponential term
items.body:
**Component / Area:** ttnn eltwise backward (composite)

**Issue Type:** Performance

## Observed

`softplus_bw` runs 9 `ttnn::` calls plus one `where` for a gradient that is a
single branch on `beta*x > threshold`:

```cpp
Tensor mul_input_beta = ttnn::multiply(input, beta, ...);
Tensor exp_beta_self = ttnn::exp(mul_input_beta, false, ...);
Tensor sub_result = ttnn::add(mul_input_beta, -threshold, ...);
Tensor temp = ttnn::multiply(
    ttnn::multiply(grad, exp_beta_self, ...),
    ttnn::reciprocal(ttnn::add(exp_beta_self, 1.0f, ...), ...), ...);
Tensor grad_result = ttnn::where(ttnn::gtz(sub_result, ...), grad, temp, ...);
```

Shipped op against a hand-built minimal that folds the redundant intermediates,
Blackhole p150b, bfloat16 2048x2048, min of 9, outputs compared element by element
with NaN treated as equal:

| | time |
|---|---|
| `ttnn.softplus_bw` as shipped | 536.4 us (7.1x clone) |
| minimal equivalent | 475.8 us, **11.3% faster** |
| outputs identical | yes |

This is the most modest of the set and I am reporting it as such.

## Expected

Fold the intermediates so the branch is evaluated once.

I would like to work on this through the bounty program.

items.title: ttnn.logit_bw compares an already-boolean mask against 1.0, costing 23% of the op
items.body:
**Component / Area:** ttnn eltwise backward (composite)

**Issue Type:** Performance

## Observed

`logit_bw` builds a 0/1 mask with `logical_and` and then compares it to 1.0:

```cpp
Tensor status = ttnn::logical_and(
    ttnn::ge(input, 0.0f, ...), ttnn::le(input, 1.0f, ...), ...);
grad_result = where(ttnn::eq(status, 1.0f, ...), grad_result, std::nanf(""));
```

`status` is the output of `logical_and`, so it is already 0/1.
`ttnn::eq(status, 1.0f)` is an identity on it and costs a full-tensor dispatch.

Shipped op against a hand-built minimal that passes `status` straight to `where`,
Blackhole p150b, bfloat16 2048x2048, min of 9, outputs compared element by element
with NaN treated as equal:

| | time |
|---|---|
| `ttnn.logit_bw` as shipped | 1543.7 us |
| minimal equivalent | 1191.5 us, **22.8% faster** |
| outputs identical | yes |

One dispatch removed, 22.8% of the op. The whole op runs 13 `ttnn::` calls plus 2
`where` for a single gradient.

## Expected

Pass `status` to `where` directly.

I would like to work on this through the bounty program.

items.title: tril / triu build the triangular mask on the host one element at a time, at 277x a clone
items.body:
**Component / Area:** ttnn eltwise unary (composite)

**Issue Type:** Performance

## Observed

Blackhole p150b, bfloat16, TILE, DRAM interleaved, min of 7.

| N | clone | `tril` | vs clone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 42.7 us | 841.8 us | 19.7x |
| 1024 | 41.0 us | 3001.2 us | 73.2x |
| 2048 | 73.3 us | 20352.2 us | **277.7x** |

`triu` is the same, 20590.0 us at N=2048. The cost grows superlinearly: doubling
N multiplies the time by 3.6x then 6.8x against 4x the data.

The multiply is not the cost. `multiply(a, a)` on the same tensor is 127.0 us,
1.8x clone. Everything above that is mask construction.

`tril` calls `index_tril<::bfloat16>`
(`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary/device/unary_composite_op.cpp:309`),
which lands in `index_trilu` at
`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/functions.hpp:57`:

```cpp
auto output_buffer = std::vector<T>(padded_shape.volume());
...
for (uint32_t itr = 0; itr < iterations; itr++) {
    for (int32_t y = 0; y < padded_shape[penultimate]; y++) {
        for (int32_t x = 0; x < padded_shape[ultimate]; x++) {
            int32_t value = (IS_UPPER) ? (x >= (y + diag)) : (y >= (x - diag));
            output_buffer[index + (y * padded_shape[ultimate]) + x] = static_cast<T>(value);
        }
    }
}
```

The whole mask is allocated and written on the host, one scalar per element, then
transferred and multiplied. At N=2048 that is 4,194,304 host writes plus an 8 MiB
transfer, for a value that is a pure function of the element coordinates.

## Expected

Generate the mask on device. `y >= (x - diag)` depends only on the coordinates,
which the reader already computes per page, so no host buffer and no transfer is
needed.

## Related, and distinct

#53971 and #52038 both concern `tril` / `triu` correctness: the mask being built
as bfloat16 whatever the input dtype, and an `inf` in the masked region becoming
NaN on the fp32 path. Both identify the mask-multiply composition. Neither reports
that the mask is built on the host or what it costs, which is what this issue is
about.

I would like to work on this through the bounty program.

items.title: KDA: `prepare_chunk_recurrence` returns a wrong `t_inv` at real decay magnitudes, breaking 68 of 69 Kimi-K3 KDA layers

labels.name: shield_prefill
labels.description: Prefill tasks worked on by Shield team

items.body:
Part of #53508.

`prepare_chunk_recurrence` returns a wrong `t_inv` — the inverse of the delta rule's UT transform —
whenever the per-chunk decay is slow enough that `N` grows to O(1). Kimi-K3 is in that regime on 68
of its 69 KDA layers, so the KDA layer's output is uncorrelated with its own torch reference there.
It is a numerical failure, not a wiring one: every input to the recurrence is exact, and the scan
downstream is exact.

## Symptom

Kimi-K3 KDA layer, 1024 tokens, real weights, **a single Blackhole card** — no mesh, no fabric, no CCL:

| layer | PCC vs `kda_forward_reference` |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99997 |
| 1 | **0.69629** |

At 8x4 over 5120 tokens the same layer scores **-0.0047**, and a 2-layer Kimi-K3 stack scores
**-0.0016** against the model's own vLLM trace (`decoder_output_layer_1`).

Layer 0 is not a counter-example, it is the tell: its decay is fast enough that `N` underflows to
~0, so `t_inv ~= I` and the transform is trivially right. It is the only one of the 69 KDA layers
in that corner.

## Root cause

`invert_doubling` (`prepare_chunk_recurrence.cpp`) evaluates

```
(I-N)^-1 = (I+N)(I+N^2)(I+N^4)(I+N^8)(I+N^16)
```

which is exact in real arithmetic and cheap — 8 tile matmuls against the 30 of the Horner path it
replaced. Its intermediates, though, are the explicit powers `N^2..N^16`. The kernel comment says
the shorter dependency chain "is also expected to improve fp32 stability, but that must be validated
empirically."

On Kimi-K3's real chunks `||N||inf` reaches **17** (median 2.4), so `||N^16||` reaches **O(1e2)**
while the inverse being computed is bounded by **1**. Those intermediates cancel, and the
cancellation costs more significant digits than the hardware carries.

In Torch, on the same real `N`:

| inversion | fp32 | bf16-rounded intermediates |
|---|---|---|
| doubling (current) | 0.00052 | **12.98856** |
| Horner (30 matmuls) | 0.00000 | **0.00227** |
| blocked 16x16 | 0.00000 | 0.06816 |

On device, no compute config recovers it — this is `t_inv` max abs error against an fp64 reference,
on real Kimi-K3 layer-1 chunks:

| | fp32_dest_acc=False | fp32_dest_acc=True |
|---|---|---|
| LoFi | 18.14 | 19.96 |
| HiFi2 | 25.98 | 64.51 |
| HiFi4 | 24.74 | **6.14** |

The best cell is the configuration `ttKDA` already runs under.

## Why no test caught it

Two independent blind spots:

1. **`t_inv` is `I + strictly-lower`**, so whole-tensor PCC is dominated by the identity diagonal.
   The broken output scored **0.99508** — above the suite's 0.999 bar on most shapes — while its
   strictly-lower part, the entire content of the transform, scored **0.935**. Thresholds on this
   output should be set on the strictly-lower part.
2. **The gate range is pinned.** `_host_inputs` builds it as `g = -0.001 - 0.05 * rand`, so every
   case runs at `|g| <= 0.051`, where `N` stays small and the high powers stay bounded. Kimi-K3's
   gate is `-5.0 * sigmoid(...)`, spanning `(-5, 0)`. Relatedly, `host_protocol` in
   `recurrent_chunk_scan_test_utils.py` pins `final_decay` to [0.86, 0.94] and the strict-lower
   block to 0.015.

The KDA layer suite covers the opposite corner: `make_kimi_k3_test_case` uses **real weights with
`torch.randn` activations**, so `test_kimi_k3_layer_1_real_weights_pcc` exercises this very layer
and passes at 0.9995. Nothing exercised real weights against real activations.

## Attribution (how it was localized)

All on real Kimi-K3 layer-1 tensors, one chip:

- The six inputs to the recurrence — q, k, v after conv+SiLU, beta, the log-decay gate, the output
  gate — all score **>= 0.99996** against torch, for both layers.
- Crossing the two recurrence stages between device and torch:

  | path | PCC vs torch prepare + torch scan |
  |---|---|
  | torch prepare -> **device scan** | **0.99999** |
  | **device prepare** -> torch scan | **0.00145** |

- Within prepare, six of seven outputs match at 1.00000; only `t_inv` is wrong.

Ruled out by measurement: dtype (forcing every preparation output to fp32 moves the end result by
4e-4; fp32 for the affine summary by 1e-5), math fidelity, chunk grouping (identical at 20/10/5/4),
sequence length (already wrong at one chunk per rank), the SP/distributed prefix (reproduces on one
chip), and the KDA state cache.

## Reproduce

```bash
export KIMI_K3_HF_MODEL=/mnt/models/blaze/moonshotai/Kimi-K3-dequantized
# one Blackhole card, ~6 s: layer 0 passes, layer 1 scores 0.696
pytest models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tests/kimi_k3/test_kda_single_device.py -s
# names the stage: device prepare 0.00145, device scan 0.99999
pytest models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tests/kimi_k3/test_kda_prepare_vs_scan.py -s
# shows no compute config rescues t_inv
pytest models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tests/kimi_k3/test_kda_tinv_precision.py -s
```

## Fix

`invert_horner` replaces the doubling product with Horner accumulation of the same nilpotent series,
`S <- I + N*S` thirty times. Its intermediates are the partial sums, bounded by the answer, so
nothing large is formed and nothing cancels. The series must be summed in full — truncating to 20
terms still errs by 0.68, since `N` is only nilpotent at the 32nd power.

Pushed to `feature/kimi-k3-modules` (`2a5d2f1bd5d`) and `feature/kimi-k3-prefill` (`005b716c1d2`).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `t_inv` strictly-lower PCC | 0.93549 | **1.00000** |
| `t_inv` max abs error | 6.1364 | **0.0102** |
| KDA layer 1, one chip | 0.69629 | **0.99988** |
| KDA layer 1, 8x4, 5120 tok | -0.00469 | **0.99990** |
| 2-layer K3 stack vs `decoder_output_layer_1` | -0.00156 | **0.99816** |

One implementation note: `N` is held in `normalized_q`, not `workspace_1` — the latter produced two
deterministic NaNs in `final_decay` at the n160 production shape, at any iteration count.

### Cost, and the open question

30 tile matmuls per chunk instead of 8. `test_prepare_chunk_recurrence_production_performance`
regresses on its smallest shape (h2-n4-k32-v64): **36.1us against a 26.7us budget**. I left it
failing rather than rebaselining it, since the kernel is genuinely slower.

At the layer level it does not show — one `ttKDA.forward` over 5120 tokens on 8x4 measured
**80.5-102.0 ms** with Horner against **88.9-116.8 ms** with doubling across three trials, with the
7168x12288 projections and host dispatch dominating and the spread swamping the difference. Those
are untraced eager calls; the traced number is the one that would settle it.

`invert_doubling` is kept in the file. If the microbenchmark matters, the cheaper options are a
`||N||` bound selecting between the two paths, or the blocked 16x16 variant above (0.068 error in
Torch, ~14 matmuls) — though 0.068 against an answer bounded by 1 is a much thinner margin than
Horner's 0.0023, and I did not validate it end-to-end.

Everything else stays green: 241/244 KDA op tests (the two `sigmoid_gated_rms_norm` perf failures
reproduce with the stock kernel on this box) and 11/11 in the KDA model layer suite.
